rule.text:
# Regime facts and the primary scope (fixed before any regime reading or count)

The paper's primary scope is "turbulent flow of a Newtonian fluid over smooth walls
under incompressible or low-Mach conditions". The facts below say, for each recorded
test, whether its flow lies inside that scope. They describe the tested flow case,
not the method.

## Items

Every design of every eligible work; every contrast that is a strict, broad or
upper-bound member; every transfer row; every constitutive candidate that has facts
(i), (ii) and (iii).

## Facts (one value per item and axis)

- `surface`
  - `smooth`: the source calls the wall on which the treatment acts smooth, or
    describes no roughness or texture on it. A smooth wall of any shape (hill, bump,
    step, aerofoil) is smooth.
  - `rough`: that wall carries roughness or texture in every repetition of the item:
    a sand-grain or equivalent roughness height, a roughness length, resolved or
    modelled roughness elements, riblets, ice roughness, a vegetation or urban canopy.
  - `both`: the item's repetitions include smooth and rough walls.
- `compressibility`
  - `low`: the source solves the incompressible equations for the case, or states a
    free-stream, bulk, inflow or reference Mach number at or below 0.3, or calls the
    case incompressible, quasi-incompressible, nearly incompressible or low-Mach.
  - `compressible`: every repetition of the item has a stated Mach number above 0.3,
    or the source calls the case transonic, supersonic or hypersonic.
  - `both`: the repetitions include both.
  - `not stated`: the source gives neither the equations nor a Mach number for the case.
- `thermal_coupling`
  - `none`: isothermal flow, or temperature or a scalar transported passively with
    constant fluid properties.
  - `coupled`: in every repetition buoyancy enters the momentum equation (natural or
    mixed convection, stable or unstable stratification), or density or viscosity
    vary with temperature or composition in the tested case (strongly heated or
    cooled walls with variable properties, supercritical fluids, reacting flow).
    Aerodynamic heating in a compressible flow is recorded under compressibility and
    is `none` here unless the source also imposes buoyancy.
  - `both`: the repetitions include both.
- `fluid`
  - `newtonian single-phase` (default);
  - `other`: non-Newtonian, multiphase, free-surface, particle-laden or
    magnetohydrodynamic flow.

`mach_stated`: the Mach number or range the source gives for the item, or null.

A located quote is required for every value `rough`, `both`, `compressible`,
`coupled` and `other`, and for `low` (the statement of incompressibility or the Mach
number). `smooth`, `none` and `newtonian single-phase` need no quote when the source
describes no roughness, no temperature effect and no other fluid.

## Derived class (script)

An axis lies outside when its value is `rough`, `compressible`, `coupled` or `other`.
An item is **outside the primary scope** when at least one axis lies outside, and
**inside** otherwise. `both` on an axis counts as inside: at least one repetition of
the item has the primary-scope value on that axis. `not stated` compressibility
counts as inside and is reported as a number.

- An eligible work is inside when at least one of its designs is inside.
- A work is a matched-contrast member inside the primary scope when at least one of
  its member contrasts of that tier is inside.
- A work is a constitutive member inside when at least one qualifying candidate is inside.
- A transfer test is inside or outside as its row.

## Scope of these facts

They classify the conditions of the recorded tests. They are not evidence about
whether any wall treatment is accurate in a regime, and a test outside the primary
scope remains a member of the collection.

clarification.text:
# Clarification R1 to the regime rule (written after the pass-3 reading)

Written on 19 November 2026 at 13:48:07 UTC, after the regime facts of all 615 items
had been read and the first counts had been computed. `regime_rule.md` is unchanged
(its SHA-256 is in `freeze_pass3.txt`). This file narrows one clause and reports the
effect.

**Clause.** "An eligible work is inside when at least one of its designs is inside."

**Clarification.** "Designs" here means designs that test a wall treatment or a stress
estimator: a design with at least one of the groups prescribed input, coupled LES,
RANS or thermal. A design recorded without such a group (a wall-resolved reference
calculation, a verification of the numerical scheme without a wall model) does not
place a work inside the primary scope. The same narrowing is already used for the
first-cell class of a work (clarification S1: a calculation that tests no treatment
"stays outside").

**Why.** N189 tests its wall model only at Mach 6 and Mach 7.7. Its record also holds
one design without a wall model, a set of scheme-verification cases that includes a
Mach 0.1 shear layer. Under the clause as first written that design alone would place
N189 inside the primary scope.

**Effect, reported with both values.** Eligible works wholly outside the primary
scope: three under the clause as first written (N054, N707, P02), four under the
clarification (also N189). No member of any group is affected, because N189 holds no
matched contrast, no constitutive candidate and no transfer test. The denominator
"eligible works inside the primary scope" is 105 as first written and 104 as
clarified. Both are stored in `results/revision/derived_memberships.json`; the paper
prints the clarified value.

**Rule applied as written elsewhere.** A prescribed roughness height makes a wall
`rough` whatever its size in wall units. Two works prescribe a small roughness height
in a pipe (N707: 0.005 mm; N188: 9e-7 m to 1 mm) and are recorded as rough. The source
gives no roughness height in wall units for either. N707 is a member of the matched
contrast group and counts as outside the primary scope on that ground alone.
